name: PLUTO (Planning, Learning, and Understanding for TOols) - Plan-and-Retrieve (P&R) / Edit-and-Ground (E&G) tool retrieval
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: NAACL 2024 (pages 975-988, Mexico City, Mexico, June 2024); DOI 10.18653/v1/2024.findings-naacl.61. Preprint: arXiv:2404.00450 (v1 Mar 30 2024).
authors_affiliation: Tenghao Huang, Dongwon Jung (University of Southern California); Vaibhav Kumar; Mohammad Kachuee; Xiang Li; Puyang Xu; Muhao Chen (University of California, Davis). The arXiv v1 PDF lists only Tenghao Huang and Dongwon Jung (USC) and Muhao Chen (UC Davis); the published ACL Anthology version adds Vaibhav Kumar, Mohammad Kachuee, Xiang Li, and Puyang Xu (likely industry / Amazon Alexa collaborators) [uncertain on the exact affiliations of the four added authors]. Lead/primary institution: USC (lead author Tenghao Huang).
code_url: https://github.com/tenghaohuang/PLUTo (Python; 3 stars, 4 commits, last updated Dec 2024; contains faiss_rm.py retriever, modules.py, descripton_optimization.py for E&G, DSP_functions.py).
maintained_repo_url: N/A (the GitHub repo is a frozen code release, not a continuously-updated paper list or leaderboard; last commit Dec 2024).
task_domain: tool-use (tool retrieval for tool-augmented LLMs); also framed as LLM tool learning / NLP retrieval (cs.CL).
problem_setting: Offline, single-query tool retrieval for tool-augmented LLMs over a large static tool pool (ToolBench / RapidAPI, 3,000+ tools across 49 categories, intra-category setting). Given a complex multi-faceted user query and an index of human-written tool descriptions, the system must shortlist the COMPLETE set of relevant tools (multiple tools per query; average ground-truth solution-path length is 4 tools). Single-agent. The framework is execution-free at retrieval time (it does not actually run tools to verify, leveraging the LLM's internal world knowledge instead). It is evaluated in both a Non-Finetuned setting (off-the-shelf dense retriever) and a Finetuned setting (retriever fine-tuned with in-batch negatives on domain data). Supervision is available via ToolBench annotated solution paths used as ground truth. 500 user queries evaluated per setting.
what_is_retrieved: tools (tool/API descriptions). Each retrievable unit is a tool description d(t); ground truth for a query is the complete set of tools on its solution path (avg ~4 tools).
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus of tool/API descriptions (a fixed ToolBench/RapidAPI tool index). However, the corpus is NOT immutable: the Edit-and-Ground paradigm rewrites (edits) under-informative tool descriptions during an offline optimization phase, so the retrievable store is a static tool set whose textual content is LLM-edited offline before inference. No agent-written episodic memory of past tasks; can be characterized as static-corpus with offline content editing (mildly HYBRID in that the index content is regenerated, not just indexed as-is).
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Completeness-oriented: the explicit goal is to recover the complete set of diverse, complementary tools a complex query needs (the paper stresses that one-time similarity retrieval 'falls short of retrieving diverse types of tools'). The query planner decomposes the query into n sub-queries and the final tool set is the UNION of per-sub-query shortlists (T = union of T_i), giving a variable-size, completeness-driven result rather than a fixed top-k of similar tools. Recall (over the full ground-truth tool set) is the primary metric. Internally a fixed top-5 candidate pool per sub-query is used before LLM selection.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based reasoning method; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain of past problem-solving cases - 'editing' here refers to tool-description optimization, not case adaptation).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is a plan-decompose + dense-retrieve + LLM-selection + tool-description-editing framework.
retrieval_unit: tool-API (a single tool represented by its textual description d(t)). The retrieval target per query is the union of such tool units across decomposed sub-queries.
index_source: Static tool corpus indexed offline (ToolBench/RapidAPI tool descriptions encoded by a dense encoder into a tool index corpus D). Construction is hybrid in content: the base index is offline, but tool descriptions are offline-edited/enriched by the Edit-and-Ground optimizer (multi-round, dev-set-recall-gated) before inference; the index is then frozen at test time.
index_structure_topology: Flat dense vector index of tool-description embeddings (dense encoder + FAISS, per repo faiss_rm.py). No dependency graph or explicit hierarchy is used in retrieval; the ToolBench intra-category structure provides a category grouping of tools but PLUTO retrieves over a flat embedding space.
retriever_type: Hybrid: a dense neural retriever (DPR / Contriever bi-encoder) for first-stage candidate shortlisting, followed by LM-likelihood re-ranking and an LLM-as-selector (predictor) stage. BM25 is used only as a baseline, not as a PLUTO component. So PLUTO = dense retrieval + LM-likelihood scoring + LLM-based predictor (retriever-agnostic / plug-and-play over DPR or Contriever).
retriever_learning_signal: Two modes. Non-Finetuned: off-the-shelf dense retriever (no training, 'none'). Finetuned: contrastive in-batch-negatives training (DPR-style cross-entropy/softmax over a positive tool d_j+ vs n sampled negative tools d_ij-) on domain query-tool pairs (similarity labels). The LM-likelihood re-ranker and the LLM planner/predictor/optimizer are prompted (no gradient training; they leverage the LLM's pretrained world knowledge). No RL / preference / value-based learning signal.
query_construction: Decomposed sub-queries: an LLM-based query planner autoregressively decomposes the complex user query Q into focused sub-queries q_1...q_n. Generation uses 'furthest reasoning with plan assessment' (Zhu et al. 2023): at each step a batch of hypothesis sub-queries is generated, clustered with prior sub-queries via K-means (TF-IDF vectors), and the sub-query most distinct from previous ones is selected, encouraging diverse, non-redundant sub-queries. Each sub-query is then encoded as the dense retrieval key. Tool-side keys are the (E&G-enriched) tool descriptions.
query_granularity: Sub-task / step-level: the query is decomposed and retrieval is performed per sub-query q_i, then unioned. This is a decomposition-driven multi-query retrieval (not a single task-level one-shot query, and not per-token); effectively trajectory/plan-level decomposition into sub-query steps.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative / adaptive within an execution-free planning loop: the planner autoregressively emits sub-queries and retrieves per sub-query, evaluating after each whether the original query Q has been satisfied (self-evaluation) and stopping when the goal is judged met. So retrieval is interleaved across the auto-generated sub-query sequence rather than a single one-shot pass, but it is execution-free (no tool execution between steps).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Planner self-assessment: after generating each sub-query q_t and its shortlist, the LLM planner evaluates (based on the current planning history) whether the original query Q has been satisfactorily achieved; if not, it proposes the next sub-query q_{t+1}, triggering another retrieval. The loop is agent-initiated/LLM-judged completion rather than a fixed schedule, token-confidence, or learned-classifier trigger.
reranking: Yes - LM-likelihood re-ranking: the first-stage dense candidate pool T_i' for each sub-query is re-ranked by an LM-likelihood score LM-likelihood(q_i, t_j) = -log P(q_i, d(t_j)). The top-5 re-ranked tools are then passed to an LLM-based predictor that selects the final relevant subset T_i. This is a generative-LM-scoring re-ranker (not a trained cross-encoder), followed by LLM selection.
retrieved_context_refinement: Rerank + LLM selection/filtering: candidate tools are LM-likelihood re-ranked, truncated to top-5 per sub-query, then an LLM predictor filters to the relevant subset (distractor filtering by the LLM). Separately, the Edit-and-Ground paradigm refines the tool DESCRIPTIONS themselves (offline enrichment) before they ever enter retrieval, which is an index-side refinement rather than a post-retrieval one.
tool_document_engineering: Central contribution (Edit-and-Ground). Tool descriptions are LLM-rewritten/expanded BEFORE indexing: an Evaluator flags under-informative tools (those whose retrieval failure count exceeds a threshold on dev set); an Optimizer then prompts an LLM with (1) the base description d(t), (2) a batch of entity-filtered relevant user queries U (LLM removes specific entities to avoid overfitting to a local batch), and (3) LLM-generated reasons R explaining why the tool is helpful for those queries, producing an enriched description d'(t) = E&G(t, d(t), U, R). Done in multiple rounds, keeping the new description only if dev-set recall improves. This is query-grounded synthetic description expansion (expanded summaries grounded in user scenarios), substantially lengthening abstract human docstrings (see Table 4 examples: Magisto, Bing Image Search, LANDR Mastering).
index_content_separation: N/A / No explicit progressive-disclosure index-vs-content split (the enriched tool description serves as both the retrievable key and the content). Tools are still represented by full (enriched) descriptions.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Static tool index sourced from ToolBench / RapidAPI Hub (real-world RESTful APIs). No live CRUD synchronization, no MCP; downstream execution-pass-rate evaluation does call real RapidAPI RESTful APIs, but the retrieval index is offline/static. The paper motivates handling 'ever-evolving tool environments' but does not implement a live-synced index.
tool_dependency_awareness: Partial / implicit. PLUTO targets multi-tool completeness for complex queries (tools that jointly address a query) via query decomposition and union of per-sub-query results, but it does NOT explicitly model inter-tool data-flow dependencies (output-of-A feeds B), shared auth, prerequisites, or a tool dependency graph. Complementarity is captured through diverse sub-query decomposition rather than an explicit dependency model.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation for downstream tool use: the final shortlisted tool set T (union over sub-queries) is provided to an LLM (ChatGPT) which then executes/uses the tools to address the query (validated via ToolBench execution pass rate against real RESTful APIs). Within PLUTO itself, retrieved candidates are consumed by the LLM predictor for selection and by the planner for next-step planning. Tool descriptions are also (offline) edited to improve retrieval, an index-side use of the LLM.
planning_integration: Plan-then-retrieve interleaved in a feedback loop: an LLM query planner decomposes the query, retrieval is performed per sub-query, the planner selects suitable tools from the retrieved set, evaluates their effectiveness, and proposes the next action - a dynamic feedback loop interlinking retrieval with refinement, evaluation, and planning. It is execution-free (no real tool execution during planning, unlike ReAct). Retrieval is woven per sub-query step within this planning loop.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-sub-query (per planning step): retrieval is interleaved at the granularity of each autoregressively-decomposed sub-query within the plan, not per-CoT-token, per-sentence, or per executed tool-call (execution-free).
adaptation_mechanism: N/A for case adaptation. The only 'adaptation' is index-side: the Edit-and-Ground Optimizer adapts/rewrites tool descriptions via LLM-prompted enrichment grounded in user queries and generated reasons (a description-optimization adaptation, not retrieved-case reuse).
retrieved_item_representation: Surface form injected is the raw (LLM-enriched) tool/API descriptions of the shortlisted tools, plus their callable signatures for downstream execution. Internally tools are dense embeddings of these descriptions.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Single tool/API (a concrete callable function with its - now LLM-enriched - description). The query side is abstracted into sub-tasks, but the retrieved unit itself stays at the individual-tool level.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Several: (1) furthest-reasoning plan assessment (K-means-based selection of the most distinct sub-query) enforces goal-oriented, non-redundant decompositions and guards against faulty planning loops / hallucinating non-existent tools; (2) LM-likelihood re-ranking plus an LLM predictor that filters the top-5 candidates to relevant tools (rejecting surface-level-similar distractors - e.g. avoiding the 'all tools contain the word Love' failure of plain similarity retrieval); (3) Edit-and-Ground enrichment narrows the semantic gap between abstract human docstrings and user queries, reducing mismatch noise. No retriever-aware adversarial SFT or explicit reflection-token mechanism.
memory_type: none (no episodic/skill/workflow/graph memory; a static, offline-edited tool corpus). The only persistent artifact is the optimized tool-description store produced by E&G.
write_back: False for task experiences. The system does NOT store solved-task trajectories/cases. There is an offline 'write' of edited tool descriptions back into the tool index during the optimization phase, but this is index curation, not experiential memory write-back; no writes occur at inference.
online_growth: No. The tool store does not grow at deployment/test time; Edit-and-Ground description editing happens during an offline optimization phase and the (enriched) index is frozen at inference. No new tools or experiences are added online.
write_back_trigger: For tool-description editing: dev-set-recall-gated / on-improvement-only - the Evaluator flags a tool as under-informative when its retrieval failure count exceeds a threshold, the Optimizer rewrites it, and the new description is committed only if dev-set retrieval recall improves over the previous round (otherwise the original is kept), across multiple rounds until a (loose, cost-bounded) stop criterion. For task/experience memory: never (no experiential write-back).
failure_experience_usage: Yes, in a limited index-curation sense: retrieval FAILURE cases drive Edit-and-Ground - tools with retrieval failure counts above a threshold are selected for description optimization, and the LLM is prompted to reason about why a tool could be relevant to the failing queries. This uses retrieval failures to correct tool descriptions; it does not store failed task trajectories as retrievable negative experiences.
memory_evolution_update: Refine-overwrite (for tool descriptions): under-informative descriptions are iteratively rewritten across rounds and overwritten only when dev-set recall improves (monotonic-improvement keep/revert), i.e. delta-refinement with a quality gate. No append-only experience log, dedup-merge, or forgetting of task memories (there is no task memory).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Tool selection is not an RL/learned policy; it is dense similarity retrieval + LM-likelihood re-ranking + prompted LLM selection within a heuristic planning loop. The optional finetuning is supervised contrastive training of the dense retriever, not a learned retrieval/selection policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent, single-framework; the optimized tool index could in principle be reused, but no cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing is proposed or evaluated.
benchmarks: ToolBench (Qin et al. 2023), intra-category setting, built on the RapidAPI Hub (3,000+ tools across 49 categories; annotated solution paths, avg length 4, used as ground truth). 500 user queries evaluated per setting. Downstream evaluation uses ToolBench's automatic execution pass rate against real-world RESTful APIs.
baselines: BM25 (lexical); ToolRetriever (the prior SOTA tool retriever from ToolBench/Qin et al. 2023, a DPR-based dense retriever) - reported with DPR and Contriever backbones, in both Non-Finetuned and Finetuned settings. PLUTO is applied on top of DPR and Contriever to show retriever-agnostic gains. Plan-and-Retrieve is also compared across LLM backbones (Llama2 vs ChatGPT variants).
key_metrics: Recall (Rec) over the ground-truth tool set; NDCG (relevance-graded, 0/1/2 human-annotated relevance scale); and downstream Pass Rate (ToolBench automatic execution metric against real RESTful APIs, using ChatGPT).
headline_result: On ToolBench intra-category, Non-Finetuned PLUTO with Contriever reaches Recall 46.57 / NDCG 82.93, outperforming the best baseline (Contriever 31.78 Rec) by +9.92 Recall points; Finetuned PLUTO with Contriever reaches Recall 48.47 / NDCG 84.73 (+5.7 Rec over the Contriever baseline 42.77). With DPR, PLUTO improves Recall from 19.58 (ToolRetriever non-finetuned) toward 36.65 (PLUTO+DPR non-finetuned). PLUTO significantly surpasses the previous SOTA (ToolRetriever) on both Recall and NDCG across settings.
ablations: Component ablation (Table 2, Recall/NDCG, both settings): PLUTO-full 46.57/82.93 (NF), 48.47/84.73 (FT). Removing Edit-and-Ground (-w/o E&G) drops to 42.55/80.70 (NF) and 44.90/81.10 (FT), showing E&G's role in enhancing what is retrieved. Removing Plan-and-Retrieve (-w/o P&R) drops to 38.12/77.60 (NF) and 47.07/81.90 (FT); P&R matters most in the Non-Finetuned setting (largest Recall hit), highlighting its importance when the retriever is off-the-shelf. The full model combining both is consistently best, evidencing synergy. Additional studies: retriever-agnostic generalization across DPR and Contriever (Table 1); LLM-backbone generalization for P&R (Fig. 3, Llama2 vs ChatGPT both improve over baselines); qualitative tool-retrieval case studies (Table 3) and before/after E&G description examples (Table 4).
evaluation_decoupling: Yes. Intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall, NDCG) are reported separately from the downstream end-to-end execution Pass Rate, decoupling retrieval quality from tool-use task success.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both: retrieval-process quality (Recall / NDCG of the retrieved tool set, with graded 0/1/2 human relevance for NDCG) plus downstream outcome quality (execution Pass Rate of actually addressing the user query via real RESTful API calls).
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: PLUTO is positioned as an execution-free paradigm: unlike ReAct-style approaches that run/verify each tool at retrieval time (expensive at scale), PLUTO uses the LLM's internal world knowledge to plan, 'guaranteeing both time and cost efficiency.' The downstream pass-rate evaluation operates under limited API budgets. The Edit-and-Ground loop is acknowledged as costly, so the authors use a relatively loose stop criterion to bound cost. No explicit latency numbers, per-query API cost, or LLM-call counts are reported. [uncertain on quantitative cost figures]
context_budget_and_selection_count: Per-sub-query: a fixed top-5 re-ranked candidate pool (T'_{i,top-5}) is fed to the LLM predictor, which selects a relevant subset T_i; the final tool set is the union over the n sub-queries (variable, completeness-driven total size). Retrieval evaluation uses Recall/NDCG over the retrieved set. No fixed global top-k token budget is stated beyond the per-sub-query top-5 candidate cap.
benchmark_construction_and_size: Uses the existing ToolBench dataset (Qin et al. 2023) rather than introducing a new benchmark: 3,000+ real RapidAPI tools across 49 categories, multi-tool queries with annotated executed solution paths (avg length 4) taken as ground truth; PLUTO focuses on the high-quality intra-category subset and evaluates 500 queries per setting. NDCG relevance labels (0/1/2) were annotated by hired graduate students. Difficulty signal: best system (PLUTO+Contriever) reaches only ~46-48 Recall, indicating complete multi-tool retrieval over this large tool space remains hard.
builds_on: Dense passage retrieval (DPR; Karpukhin et al. 2020) and Contriever (Izacard et al. 2022) as retriever backbones; LM-likelihood scoring (Song/RestGPT et al. 2023); furthest reasoning with plan assessment (Zhu et al. 2023) for sub-query decomposition; adaptive/active retrieval-augmented generation (FLARE - Jiang et al. 2023; Yoran et al. 2023 robustness to irrelevant context) for the adaptive planning idea; ToolBench / ToolLLM (Qin et al. 2023) for the tool set, benchmark, and the ToolRetriever SOTA baseline; tool-documentation insights (Hsieh et al. 2023) and LLM-as-optimizer (Yang et al. 2023) motivating Edit-and-Ground.
contrasts_with: Conventional one-time 'Retrieve-and-Read' tool retrieval relying solely on similarity matching (Gorilla/Patil et al. 2023; ToolLLM/Qin et al. 2023), which the paper argues retrieves surface-similar but functionally incomplete tools and cannot handle complex multi-tool queries; ReAct (Yao et al. 2022) and execution-based planning that run/verify tools at retrieval time (expensive); and approaches that finetune on static tool sets (brittle in evolving tool environments). PLUTO instead is execution-free, plan-driven, and edits tool descriptions.
lineage: Group E (tool-use): tool-retrieval line. A 2024 work advancing tool retrieval from one-shot similarity matching toward (a) query-decomposition + iterative planning retrieval (Plan-and-Retrieve) and (b) LLM-based tool-documentation enrichment (Edit-and-Ground) to close the query-tool semantic gap. Sits alongside completeness/diversity-oriented tool retrieval (e.g. COLT) and tool-documentation works (Hsieh et al. 2023), and is a precursor to later query-planning + document-engineering tool-retrieval methods; builds on the ToolBench/ToolLLM ecosystem and adaptive-RAG ideas.
